shoal_entry.speaker: narrator
shoal_entry.text: On Day Two Hundred Fifteen, Yue reached the outer shoal with salt in the seams of her coat and the sixth-stage certificate folded among her own papers. The road from Lark Pass had taken its booked time. She could now circulate through six primary pairs. Her tested useful work remained much smaller than the harbor before her. Beyond the receiving posts, boats leaned in wooden cradles while men argued about which tide had made them lean.

shoal_e01_arrival_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_arrival_01.text: The harbor did not smell like the canal. Tar, old fish, hot metal and wet cedar competed with the clean wind from the open water. A boy dragged a length of discarded cord between two posts, making a pretend barrier. An older girl stepped over it without paying his announced toll. He called her a smuggler. She said he had not inspected the cord. Yue laughed before remembering she still needed to find the real receiving line.

shoal_e01_arrival_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_arrival_02.text: A woman behind the line held up one hand. Sui Yan had recognized Yue before Yue recognized the captain's cropped grey hair. Neither claimed the other had remained unchanged since their earlier harbor work. Sui asked for the new travel cover and current application record. Yue set them down. Six earned pairs did not replace an entry inspection, especially when something in her pack might belong to another institution.

shoal_e01_arrival_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_arrival_03.text: 'I can accept a half-unit over four ordinary breaths,' Yue said. 'A quarter-unit of useful work, with the release independently stopped and grounded. My recovered throughput is still no more than an eighth per breath.' Sui read the shoulder restriction beneath the figures. Waist work only; no sudden overhead catch. The captain tapped that line. 'Keep the page where the supervisor can see it. People hear sixth stage and begin inventing a stronger worker.'

shoal_e01_arrival_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_arrival_04.text: Sui introduced the outer shoal as a working district, not a discarded corner of the old harbor. Its salvage yard recovered timber, fittings and cargo under their actual ownership records. The new Six-Reach association wanted a local freight-signal station there. It did not own the quarantine service, the migrant wage bond or the boats in their cradles. Every new agreement would have to say which institution paid and which person could refuse.

shoal_e01_arrival_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_arrival_05.text: Han Pei was sorting arrival slips beneath an awning. He had used a broken oar as a paper weight and written its owner on a tag, which amused Yue until he explained that the owner kept looking for it. A second arrival had offered a whole boat hook as a weight. Han had declined. By afternoon, the receiving table would have resembled a shrine to missing equipment if he accepted every useful thing without asking how it returned.

shoal_e01_arrival_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_arrival_06.text: He checked Yue's invitation to a work interview. A new outer-shoal arrival grant, approved for this receiving, covered eight nights of room and meals at two copper a day. Sixteen copper paid that stay; eight covered the defined interview and receipt work. It was separate from the coming employment offer and any Lark payment. Accepting the arrival arrangement would neither enroll her in a job nor oblige her to lend her cultivated channels to a port experiment.

shoal_e01_arrival_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_arrival_07.text: 'Two lodgings have accepted the same room-and-meal price,' Han said. 'The receiving-house guest bed and the upstairs inn room. You can decide after the interview. Both have a checked ordinary exit.' Yue asked whether refusing the offered work would turn the eight nights into a debt. It would not. Han showed her the clause without improving it into a speech about generosity. Someone had once proposed the debt. The board had crossed it out.

shoal_e01_arrival_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_arrival_08.text: A gull landed on the awning and shook water onto Han's sleeve. He moved the papers first, then his arm. Yue asked why the arrival office stood so far from the main stores. Sui answered that fire separation and quarantine separation happened to agree on that particular distance. Beyond the yard, blackened stones formed an interrupted rectangle beside a newer warehouse. The space had not been rebuilt. Yue could see grass between its foundation blocks.

shoal_e01_arrival_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_arrival_09.text: 'The old lamp store burned there,' Sui said. 'Three workers got out. A fourth was injured and left harbor work afterwards. The new building was put elsewhere.' She did not offer the man's name for Yue's notebook. The captain had inspected the site, not received permission to tell every part of his life. Yue looked again at the grass. An empty foundation could warn someone without turning a survivor into its permanent explanation.

shoal_e01_arrival_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_arrival_10.text: Qin Shuo arrived carrying a small wooden cash box and no keys to the old wage bond. Today's receiving belonged to the new association account. He said so before opening the box. Yue liked him better for the unnecessary-looking distinction. It would matter later if somebody wanted the old promise to pay a new expense. He was serving as this arrival grant's named receiver for two hours, with another clerk taking over after the interview.

shoal_e01_arrival_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_arrival_11.text: Across the yard, Rong Sui watched two packers roll a charcoal barrel away from a tar shed. The factor wore a coat Yue remembered from forest work, repaired with a darker strip down one sleeve. He greeted her cordially and asked whether Lark's method had finally solved their contact problem. Yue said she had brought a result with conditions. Rong sighed. 'Conditions travel better than solutions,' he said. 'Unfortunately I can sell fewer of them.'

shoal_e01_arrival_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_arrival_12.text: Yan Su stopped beside them with a rope over his shoulder. He had come to collect ordinary crew work, not to test Yue's new stage. His workers were lowering an empty mast onto trestles. The heavy end belonged to their tackle and cleared lifting crew. Yue stepped outside its marked sweep without being told twice. Yan smiled at that, and Rong looked impatient. She wondered which response would appear in the afternoon's account of her usefulness.

shoal_e01_arrival_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_arrival_13.text: The invitation offered access to the receiving table. What she could put on that table depended on the terms she had actually chosen at Lark. Public comparison pages, a licensed appendix and loan kit, or an independent dispatch were different things. The captain would record the actual permission before directing her toward a bench. Yue unfastened the travel cover and kept her own bodily practice book inside her pack.

shoal_e01_lark_gate.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_lark_gate.text: Han found the Lark receiving line and asked Yue to read its scope aloud. The old work wages had already settled before departure. This carried arrangement concerned the particular pages, property or dispatch now being received. No one could convert it into a continuing labor appointment because her body had arrived with it. Yue named the actual terms before the clerk touched anything in the cover.

shoal_e01_common_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_common_01.text: Yue laid out the consented public comparison pages. Their owners had permitted that method to be read and copied with its conditions. No private appendix or portable reference kit had accompanied the choice. Han checked the headings, dates and offered names before making the receiving note. Rong leaned across the table to ask where the improved geometry lay. Yue pointed to the public drawing. 'Here, to the extent its owners chose to show it.'

shoal_e01_common_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_common_02.text: He wanted the measurements behind a narrower set of contact teeth. They were not on the public pages. Yue did not invent them from the shape of the drawing or call absence a proof of concealment. The pages described how Lark's workers had separated a usable contact from a claim about performance. A port builder could learn from that comparison. To use a particular supplier's protected design, the builder would need that supplier's permission.

shoal_e01_common_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_common_03.text: Rong had expected to show her the private bench that afternoon. He closed its appointment book instead. The available public method did not include a right to use his experimental fixture or publish its settings. 'Then we read at the open table,' Han said. 'No kit needs a custody entry.' Yue felt the change as a door closing. She had chosen public access at Lark and could not arrive here expecting every private door to open in congratulations.

shoal_e01_common_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_common_04.text: The open table stood under a sound awning near the arrival office. Its tools were a ruler, a straight wooden edge and a cheap copper contact strip owned by the port school. A teacher had lent them for the named reading and wanted them back before evening. They were not the calibrated Lark kit. Yan Su brought an empty signal housing for comparison, with its fuel socket blocked and its loose lid tied down.

shoal_e01_common_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_common_05.text: Yue asked a packer to move the wooden edge across the drawing while she read the conditions. The woman moved it too far and said the stroke looked like a crab. Yan replied that crabs could at least stop without waiting for a supplier. The packer laughed, then shifted the edge to its actual reference line. Ordinary hands had made a useful comparison. The joke did not turn the school's tools into a field-qualified device.

shoal_e01_common_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_common_06.text: Two workers who could not have entered Rong's supplier room joined the reading. One had lost an hour yesterday when a freight lamp gave an uncertain signal; the other wanted the shared warning to be audible from her packing table. They described their own work, not the hidden cause of either failure. Yue wrote the offered questions on a separate sheet. The public method had changed who could speak beside it without promising an answer beyond its measurements.

shoal_e01_common_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_common_07.text: Rong listened from the edge of the awning. He said a comparison with borrowed school tools would not satisfy his customer. Yue agreed. The useful part today was identifying what needed a trained port test, including the condition of the contact housing and its actual fuel feed. Rong looked less pleased by agreement than he might have looked by an argument. A disagreement would have let him accuse her of preferring a cheap drawing to working equipment.

shoal_e01_common_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_common_08.text: Han asked whether the workers wanted their questions included in the receiving packet. One agreed under her name. The other offered a question without a personal attribution and retained her own account. The clerk respected both choices. Yue did not need the woman to become a witness in order to learn that the table was too far from the signal bell. A usable public method could improve an inquiry while leaving some ordinary experience outside its record.

shoal_e01_common_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_common_09.text: Sui checked the reading's equipment return before the afternoon line grew. The teacher received the ruler, edge and contact strip in their recorded condition. No private board, appendix or future bench slot appeared in Yue's property list. The captain kept the open-table reading separate from formal port entry. It had taken place in the outer receiving district, under its named permission, without admitting a passenger or object past the quarantine boundary.

shoal_e01_common_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_common_10.text: At the empty signal housing, Yan asked Yue to point out the release stroke on the public diagram. She did it without connecting a trace. Her body's limit would matter when they eventually reached a qualified test, but no qi was needed to trace a line with a finger. Yan said he preferred a worker who could name the exit before wanting to prove the entrance. Yue said she still wanted to prove it. He laughed and said that was evident.

shoal_e01_common_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_common_11.text: The public packet remained available at the open receiving table under its offered scope. It could travel into the later port inquiry as a permitted comparison, with its missing supplier geometry clearly named. Yue took her own note back; the source pages stayed in the clerk's temporary custody until their agreed return. The two workers left for their ordinary jobs. Their presence had been the gain she chose. The private bench remained unavailable.

shoal_e01_common_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_common_12.text: Rong offered to discuss a separately licensed bench appointment later if his current booking allowed it. Yue did not accept a future term inside today's public reading. He would send an actual offer, and she could examine its price and scope then. For now, her Lark arrangement had supplied public pages and no equipment loan. She went back to Qin's interview chair with a better question and a loss she could name without pretending it was somebody else's fault.

shoal_e01_lease_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_lease_01.text: Yue set the waxed stop cover on the table before opening the kit. The adjustable zero-load contact board and external copper comparison strip belonged to the Lark association. The private appendix licensed supplier freight-signal geometry, not Yue's bodily routes. Han checked those items against the travel list without touching the settings. A loan could permit possession and still place limits on what happened after the lid opened.

shoal_e01_lease_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_lease_02.text: Rong recognized the supplier's seal and moved his appointment book closer. The license allowed the appendix to be read at the inspected supplier bench during Days Two Hundred Fifteen through Two Hundred Sixty-Five. It did not permit copying the private pages. Actual bench work would still need the port's entry clearance and the supervisor's present conditions. The current receiving was an inventory check in the outer district. No fuel or stone had arrived inside the kit.

shoal_e01_lease_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_lease_03.text: Han named the licensed return carrier and the Day Two Hundred Sixty-Six receiving deadline. A condition receipt at that carrier would transfer the kit into the agreed return route. It would not mean the lender had already received it at Lark. Yue repeated the distinction before signing. She would keep the item list with its next-day check, and a damaged cover would be reported rather than quietly replaced with a prettier cloth.

shoal_e01_lease_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_lease_04.text: The supervisor showed her the supplier room from its clear doorway. A folded board on the bench marked its current stop position. The room had an ordinary exit to the yard; its fuel cabinet was shut. Yue could see the field work she wanted to try and the parts she had not yet been authorized to touch. Her six primary pairs did not change the room's permission. She left the borrowed kit closed until the actual test appointment.

shoal_e01_lease_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_lease_05.text: Rong asked whether the private appendix's contact geometry could be shown to the packing crews. Yue said the license allowed their defined comparison at the bench, not a public copy or an improvised lecture outside. Any permitted participant needed the owner's accepted scope. Public safety warnings would still be issued independently. A private method could not conceal a hazardous operating condition, but that rule did not make every commercial diagram public property.

shoal_e01_lease_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_lease_06.text: He seemed relieved by the first answer and wary of the second. Yue understood why. A private bench could offer a useful piece of work without granting its owner control over every resulting safety question. Rong wanted her to remember the arrangement as access. She wanted to remember the terms that made access honest. Han let their silence last while he tied the appendix cover. The silence belonged to them, not to a clerk's duty to make agreement pleasant.

shoal_e01_lease_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_lease_07.text: Yan brought an empty freight-signal housing to the outer table. It would later be compared under qualified direction, with the separate source and release recorded. For now, he pointed out two incompatible bolt marks. The private appendix might help distinguish which geometry had been used. It could not tell them whose hand last adjusted the old housing. Yue copied only the publicly offered item condition, leaving the protected drawing inside its cover.

shoal_e01_lease_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_lease_08.text: Two packers waited beyond the supplier doorway and asked whether they would be allowed to watch the later test. Rong said he would consider their named places with the bench supervisor. Neither had a present invitation. Yue felt the loss in that answer: the licensed room would let her see more of one design while keeping some workers outside. She asked Han to retain their request instead of claiming a single cleared observer could represent everybody's experience.

shoal_e01_lease_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_lease_09.text: Han retained the offered requests and gave each worker a receiving slip. One woman tore hers in half by mistake while folding it. He issued a replacement with the old slip canceled rather than calling the tear a second request. The small repair made the woman smile. Yue needed the moment. She had begun to imagine that every permission question would make people stiff and ceremonial. The people still had hands, pockets and accidents.

shoal_e01_lease_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_lease_10.text: Sui inspected the kit's outer case and recorded its present quarantine position. It remained in the named secure receiving cupboard until the port cleared its entry. Yue held the cupboard receipt, not an imaginary right to carry the kit anywhere the map offered a bench. The private appendix stayed sealed beside it. The license was real, the later appointment was possible, and neither had yet become a performed field application.

shoal_e01_lease_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_lease_11.text: Rong pencilled the first proposed bench interval after entry clearance. The supervisor would confirm it after the arriving items passed their actual checks. Yue kept the proposal separate from paid employment. Lark's loan was property permission, not an old labor contract following her to the shoal. If the port wanted her work, it would have to hire that work under its own source, hours and safe limits.

shoal_e01_lease_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_lease_12.text: She returned to Qin's interview chair with the condition list and cupboard receipt. The public table had fewer questions from workers than it might have had if she had brought only open pages. Her chosen license had made a private comparison possible and narrowed who could use its particulars. By Day Two Hundred Sixty-Six, the borrowed kit would need an actual receiver. Until then, every useful thing she learned would still have an owner and a scope.

shoal_e01_witness_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_witness_01.text: Yue offered the independent dispatch instead of a reference kit. Its receiving instructions named the outer-shoal desk and required actual receipt by Day Two Hundred Seventeen. Han checked the seal against the letter's offered identifier, then signed today's completed delivery. The dispatch remained a source under its owner's permission. It did not grant her a private bench, equipment loan or a claim to copy any protected appendix merely because she had carried its cover.

shoal_e01_witness_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_witness_02.text: The separately earmarked six-copper Lark dispatch payment became due after that receipt. Qin released it through the agreed receiving arrangement and returned the acknowledgment for the actual paying source. The new port arrival grant did not fund it. Yue put the six copper in her own purse. A completed small job could buy real meals. It did not restore the optional equipment booking she had missed when choosing the independent dispatch.

shoal_e01_witness_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_witness_03.text: Rong asked where the portable board had gone. Yue told him it had stayed out of her arrangement. There was no kit in her pack and no private appendix in the dispatch. He closed the tentative supplier-bench line he had left for an equipment arrival. The result was sharp enough to feel personal. Yue had selected independence at Lark. She could not now accuse the port of withholding property that had never been offered on her route.

shoal_e01_witness_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_witness_04.text: Han opened the dispatch only within its receiving instructions. Its offered account concerned the method's recorded stop and comparison conditions, with an independent observer's question attached. Rong wanted the observer to confirm that one supplier's contact teeth had caused the failure. The paper did not say so. Yue refused to strengthen it from memory. She could answer for carrying the sealed source and its actual receipt, not for the conclusion somebody wished its seal contained.

shoal_e01_witness_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_witness_05.text: A packer listening beside the table asked whether an independent dispatch was a complaint. Han said it depended on what the offered source actually asked. The woman considered that answer, then offered her own question about a warning that could not be heard through tar barrels. Yue wrote it separately with her permission. Delivering another person's paper had put Yue in the conversation. It had not given her authority to absorb the woman's experience into the dispatch.

shoal_e01_witness_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_witness_06.text: Rong said the supplier room was reserved for an equipment comparison this week. Without the borrowed board, he had no present bench place for her. Yan instead offered a walk around the outside of the empty signal housing after his crew finished lowering the mast. It would be an ordinary observation, with the fuel socket blocked. Yue accepted that finite invitation. She would have fewer technical particulars and more distance from the supplier's preferred story.

shoal_e01_witness_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_witness_07.text: They waited for the mast to settle on both trestles before crossing the marked sweep. Yan asked the crew to check the tackle's unloaded line. Yue kept her arms below the shoulder limit and carried only the offered condition sheet. She was relieved that nobody asked her to demonstrate a sixth-stage catch. The ordinary crew had lowered a heavy object with equipment. Her useful task was arriving after it could no longer fall.

shoal_e01_witness_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_witness_08.text: At the housing, she could see two old bolt marks and a later bright scrape. Yan could identify the surfaces he had actually handled, and refused to assign the other marks to a named worker. The private geometry would have made a different comparison possible, but she did not possess it. She recorded the visible condition under its offered scope. Independent work could be narrower than licensed work and still keep somebody's unsupported certainty out of the account.

shoal_e01_witness_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_witness_09.text: Han retained the delivered source with its actual custody line. Yue kept her own wage acknowledgment and travel note. No equipment return date appeared because no equipment had been borrowed. The missed booking remained on the Lark account where it belonged. She would not return an imaginary board at the end of a term to make the route look as productive as another arrangement.

shoal_e01_witness_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_witness_10.text: Sui asked whether the dispatch required any continued labor. It did not. Today's receiving completed the paid carried task. Any later port inquiry would have to invite Yue separately, and any new paid work would need the port's own appropriation. The captain wrote the completed date before sending the protected source to its named local receiver. The source travelled a few careful steps farther than its messenger, with a signed handover instead of an assumption.

shoal_e01_witness_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_witness_11.text: Rong wanted to speak privately after the interview. Yue said he could offer a conversation; it would not give him the right to decide what she had delivered or which workers she might hear later. He smiled as though the distinction were amusing. She could not tell whether he enjoyed her caution or had already found a way to sell it. The uncertainty was something she would have to live with until he did another actual thing.

shoal_e01_witness_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_witness_12.text: She returned to Qin's interview chair without a kit receipt or private bench appointment. Six copper paid the completed dispatch. The unchosen equipment slot had been lost, and a separately offered outside observation had taken its place. She could hear the packing woman's question from the table behind her. Independence had made that question easier to receive. It had also left a technical comparison she could not perform today.

shoal_e01_rejoin_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_rejoin_01.text: Qin asked the same first question she would have asked an uncertified traveler. Where would Yue sleep if she declined the harbor's offer? Yue had priced two licensed houses beyond the quarantine fence. Their rates covered the arrival grant's eight nights. After that, her own settled road money could buy a short extension. She would not accept an indefinite promise of a room in exchange for being useful whenever someone knocked.

shoal_e01_rejoin_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_rejoin_02.text: The proposed salvage job came from the new Outer Shoal Restoration Appropriation. Four hundred eighty copper funded one narrow six-week operation: one hundred fifty for Yue's thirty five-copper shifts, one hundred eighty for a qualified supervisor, sixty for materials, fifty for dispatch, and forty held for ordinary care. Qin put an untouched acceptance line beneath the terms. If Yue accepted later, the scheduled shifts would run from Day Two Hundred Thirty-Two through Day Two Hundred Seventy-Three.

shoal_e01_rejoin_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_rejoin_03.text: That sum did not employ every person Yue could see. The riggers, fire crews, cooks, and quarantine hands retained their separate employers and wages. A restoration supervisor could authorize the funded unloaded comparisons and reject unsafe work; the appointment could not redirect the harbor's entire labor force. Yue circled the distinction herself. She had seen a modest purse become a limitless obligation simply because a useful person stood beside it.

shoal_e01_rejoin_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_rejoin_04.text: He Ming joined them carrying a wrapped bowl rather than a committee seal. His packing shift ended at noon, and he wanted to collect his repaired kettle before the smith closed. He could show Yue the receiving-house lodging on the way. The house had a guest bed and common meals, not a right to read its residents' letters. People who slept there chose separately whether they spoke at tomorrow's public introduction.

shoal_e01_rejoin_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_rejoin_05.text: The other lodging stood above a net seller's shop. An exterior stair led to its upper rooms, and its posted keeper slept downstairs beside the street door. Couriers often took the small tables there. Rong had described it as quieter, which He Ming said was true until the couriers arrived. Yue preferred an honest noise schedule to a promise of peace. Both keepers would have to show her the second ordinary exit before payment.

shoal_e01_rejoin_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_rejoin_06.text: Qin's eight-copper interview allocation paid specified receiving work, not an advance on the proposed salvage wage. She read the names and hours aloud, including her own two-hour receipt duty. Neither choice of bed increased it. Neither required Yue to take the six-week post. He Ming ate from his bowl while she explained this, occasionally correcting the location of a house when the clerk used an old street name.

shoal_e01_rejoin_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_rejoin_07.text: Outside the chair circle, a little girl laid shells in a row and charged a pebble to cross them. Her brother refused because the tide would soon own the road. Their argument sounded grander than the table's careful terms. Yue watched them while deciding what she could actually promise. Eight nights was a beginning. It was not a family, a new profession, or permission to use everyone she met as a witness.

shoal_e01_rejoin_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_rejoin_08.text: He Ming offered to walk to either door. He would point out the places where evening carts made the lane difficult and then leave Yue to inspect the room. Rong's courier contacts might help her learn how bookings failed. The receiving house might help her hear how such failures arrived at a kitchen. Yue could not stay in both beds. The cost was equal; the people whose ordinary hours she would share were different.

shoal_e01_lodging_choice.speaker: lin_yue
shoal_e01_lodging_choice.text: Yue had two inspected rooms available for the same eight-night grant. The receiving house offered a guest bed among working households, with shared meals and their own speaking rules. The upstairs inn offered a separate room near the courier tables, with quieter mornings and commercial booking conversations. After these eight nights, either extension would need her own payment. She chose the people whose daily interruptions she could accept.

choices.text: Stay at the receiving house and share its ordinary meals.
Take the upstairs inn room beside the courier tables.

shoal_e01_guest_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_guest_01.text: He Ming took the longer lane around a cart queue. At the receiving house, its keeper showed Yue a ground-floor guest bed separated from the family sleeping room by a wooden screen. The rear door opened into an inspected public alley. No one had to cross a private bedroom to reach it. Yue tested the latch with the keeper's permission, then signed for the eight nights from Day Two Hundred Fifteen through Day Two Hundred Twenty-Two.

shoal_e01_guest_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_guest_02.text: The sixteen-copper lodging payment went to the keeper against those dates. He Ming did not take a referral fee. At supper, his sister asked whether Yue ate fish bones, then laughed when Yue treated it as a question about religious practice. A room could become intimate by accident. Before the dishes were cleared, the keeper said the bed did not make Yue a household delegate. He Ming would speak for his own packing group.

shoal_e01_guest_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_guest_03.text: A young resident who repaired sail ties wanted to know whether the proposed salvage work would replace paid hands with cultivators. Yue had no accepted post and no authority to announce staffing. She showed the narrow proposal instead of reassuring him beyond it. He read the thirty shifts slowly and returned the page. He would attend the public introduction if his morning work finished. That was a choice he kept.

shoal_e01_guest_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_guest_04.text: After supper, a woman moved a basket of mended sleeves away from the only dry wall. She made room for Yue's coat without offering to wash it. Yue asked which pump visitors could use and carried her own water. The household's kindness had a scale and a price in time. A guest who mistook every helpful gesture for an invitation would soon turn a shared house into unpaid lodging labor.

shoal_e01_guest_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_guest_05.text: The courier inn's evening conversation went on without her. Rong sent a brief notice that the booking clerk would answer formal requests at the quay, and there would be no reserved chair for Yue in the upstairs room. She accepted the inconvenience. At the receiving house, residents could explain a missed dispatch in their own hours. Commercial sources would require a separate appointment, with no assumption that a public meal supplied them.

shoal_e01_guest_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_guest_06.text: Before sleeping, Yue wrote the keeper's exit directions on a scrap she could find in the dark. She kept the household's private names out of her working notebook. Through the screen came a disagreement about a kettle lid, followed by someone giving up and lending a different lid. She would hear more of these ordinary disputes than the courier prices. The room was useful precisely because the people in it had lives beyond her questions.

shoal_e01_inn_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_inn_01.text: The inn keeper showed Yue the narrow upper room and its exterior stair. A second ordinary exit crossed an open landing to a licensed rear stair, clear of the net seller's drying frames. Yue tried both routes while it was light. The keeper entered eight paid nights, Day Two Hundred Fifteen through Day Two Hundred Twenty-Two, at the agreed sixteen copper. The room's bolt worked. Its window overlooked a yard rather than somebody else's sleeping space.

shoal_e01_inn_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_inn_02.text: He Ming carried nothing upstairs for her until she asked him to hold the door. He said the receiving house would still welcome a properly arranged visit, but supper there belonged to its residents and guests. Yue could not arrive every evening as an unpaid ninth mouth. She thanked him and set a later public appointment instead. Choosing privacy meant losing the easy hours when household questions appeared while plates were being cleared.

shoal_e01_inn_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_inn_03.text: Downstairs, two couriers compared canceled bookings without telling Yue whose cargo had been refused. She asked permission before listening. One offered to describe the booking sequence after his employer's private prices were removed; the other declined. The inn keeper allowed conversation at a table only until the net seller needed its surface for repairs. Yue would gain commercial access in fragments, under the same ordinary interruptions that governed everyone else's meal.

shoal_e01_inn_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_inn_04.text: Rong left a note offering a short booking conversation at the inn the following evening. It was an invitation to discuss current requests, not permission to inspect supplier records or a revival of any unchosen equipment appointment. Yue marked the scope beside the date. Commercial hospitality often made a future request feel agreed before it had been stated. Her separate door helped her leave a conversation without also leaving her bed.

shoal_e01_inn_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_inn_05.text: The quiet room let her check her own shoulder and grip without performing strength for curious spectators. She used no qi to test the stair rail or household fittings. On the landing, a child carried a tray too wide for the turn; Yue held the ordinary door while the keeper guided him through. No certificate was needed for that task. She wrote down the tray obstruction and gave the note to the person who could change it.

shoal_e01_inn_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_inn_06.text: After dark, the courtyard tables filled with people who knew shipping distances and disagreed about weather. Their stories could help her understand a missed receipt, but they did not stand for the households beyond the quay. Yue would have to visit those households by invitation. She slept with her pack under the bed and her working notes inside it. The inn gave her a private pause between requests, with fewer unplanned chances to hear what home had cost someone.

shoal_e01_close_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_close_01.text: By the next morning, the receiving table had been dismantled for unloading. Only a chalk rectangle showed where Qin's chair had stood. Yue waited outside the quarantine boundary with the other new arrivals. A gull tried to pull thread from a rope end and abandoned the attempt when a dock hand moved it. The harbor's ordinary work resumed around their paperwork. An interview had not given any of them permission to wander into an active quay.

shoal_e01_close_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_close_02.text: On Day Two Hundred Sixteen, Sui's clerk checked Yue's travel dates against the scheduled road stops. Yue supplied her own route and symptoms without speaking for the people who had shared the carrier. The clerk scheduled formal port entry for Day Two Hundred Twenty-Three, after the observation interval. She could walk the licensed outer lanes meanwhile. A family farther down the queue had a different date because their arrival had been later.

shoal_e01_close_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_close_03.text: Song Mei's name appeared on a public performance board, beside an afternoon slot still marked provisional. Yue remembered her as someone who could decide whether an audience deserved her story. The notice promised neither a private meeting nor an endorsement of the restoration work. Yue copied the public date and left the private contact line untouched. She hoped to hear the performance if it happened. Hope was easier to carry than an appointment made on another person's behalf.

shoal_e01_close_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_close_04.text: The next six days required ordinary patience. Yue washed her road clothes, bought thread from the net seller, and asked for the current public map of lanes outside quarantine. She did not start the proposed paid salvage shifts. The interview's figures remained a proposal. When someone called her the new harbor examiner, she corrected the title before it spread. She had arrived with a certificate and a pack, and had not yet accepted a port job.

shoal_e01_close_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_close_05.text: At dusk on Day Two Hundred Twenty-Two, she returned the map to its owner and checked tomorrow's receiving time. Her eight paid nights ended in the morning. She kept enough of her own settled savings for a short lodging extension at the posted rate while the employment decision remained open. Neither the inn nor the receiving house had agreed to indefinite free board. The keeper wanted an answer about the next night before breakfast.

shoal_e01_close_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_close_06.text: Yue packed the coat that had dried at last. In the outer yard, a worker measured a damaged timber with the same care another might give a pulse. Beyond him, the burned store's surviving wall caught the final light. Formal entry would bring Yue closer to those structures and to the people paid to handle them. It would also make the boundaries less abstract. She checked the ordinary release stroke once, without sending qi into any harbor object.

shoal_e01_exit.speaker: narrator
shoal_e01_exit.text: Before lying down, she counted the times she had answered a request merely because someone recognized her name. The list included a genuine invitation, a mistaken title, and a child needing a door held. They deserved different answers. Tomorrow she would enter under Sui's ordinary quarantine authority. Her cultivation certificate could describe tested bodily work. It could not substitute for the harbor's consent or erase another worker's own obligations.
